entities.summary:
The Siege of Nicaea was a pivotal event in the capture of the Byzantine capital, Nicaea, by the Seljuk Turks in 1097. This marked the beginning of the end of the Byzantine Empire's control over Western Anatolia. The siege was led by the Seljuk general Kilij Arslan I and resulted in the capture of the city after a brief battle. The fall of Nicaea had a lasting impact on the region, paving the way for the Seljuk Empire's expansion into Eastern Europe and the Middle East.

The significance of the Siege of Nicaea cannot be overstated. It was a turning point in the history of the Byzantine Empire, marking the beginning of the end of its control over Western Anatolia. The siege was a strategic victory for the Seljuk Turks, who went on to conquer much of Eastern Europe and the Middle East. The fall of Nicaea also had a lasting impact on the region, leading to the establishment of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum.

The legacy of the Siege of Nicaea can be seen in the subsequent history of the region. The Seljuk Empire went on to play a major role in the development of Eastern Europe and the Middle East, leaving a lasting legacy in the form of architecture, art, and culture. The siege also marked the beginning of the end of the Byzantine Empire's control over Western Anatolia, paving the way for the rise of the Ottoman Empire.

As the great historian Steven Runciman once wrote, 'The capture of Nicaea was a blow from which the Byzantine Empire never fully recovered.' The siege was a pivotal moment in the history of the region, marking the beginning of a new era of Turkish dominance.
